description: Connects this chat to the host's own WordPress site. Side effect: it creates a connect link that the host must open and approve in their own browser — until they do, nothing is connected; no password is seen or stored. Needs `session_id` and `url`. If this connector already knows the site from an earlier chat, the answer says so with `known_site`, `connected_at` and a sentence to repeat to the host, and asks whether to continue with it. A takeover needs the host's yes AND the one-time `reuse_token` the connector showed in the chat that approved the site: call it again with the same `url`, `reuse: true` and that code. Without the code the host approves once more in their own browser, which proves ownership. Naming a site alone never reuses it.

reuse.description: true when the host confirmed to continue with a site this connector remembers AND gives the one-time reuse_token from the chat that approved it. Without the code nothing is reused: the host approves once more in their own browser, which proves ownership.

reuse_token.description: Only with this call" and reuse=true: the one-time code the connector showed in the chat that connected this site. It proves the caller is the host. A hash of it is enough for the server; a wrong or missing code means no takeover.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

url.description: The WordPress address (seite). With was=handoff: the host's WordPress address to point the handover link at.

name: wi_connect_wordpress_woocommerce_site
title: Connect the host's WordPress site
